## Goal

A repository where good, modular, verified code is the path of least resistance, before any product code: every gate from REPO_STANDARDS running locally and in CI, the governance files, the agent documentation skeleton, and the protocol package's foundation (IDs, revisions, diagnostics) that every later package builds on.

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- all of [REPO_STANDARDS.md](../REPO_STANDARDS.md): workspace, catalogs, Turborepo, Biome and ESLint, tsc project references, Vitest, Playwright scaffold, dependency-cruiser rules for the package map, knip, size-limit, API Extractor, publint, attw, the license audit (OSI-only core, `pnpr/` excluded), cargo workspace with fmt, clippy and deny, lefthook, the CI plan and jobs, Renovate, CodeQL, Scorecard;
- governance files (Apache-2.0, NOTICE, DCO CONTRIBUTING, GOVERNANCE, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SECURITY);
- root and package `AGENTS.md` skeletons, `docs/agents/` playbooks and the `pnpm gen` generators;
- the `@mostra/protocol` package's foundations: ID types, dated-revision negotiation types, the diagnostic schema, and the generator that turns diagnostic codes into docs pages and a catalog;
- schema snapshot tests that fail on non-additive changes (HO-07).

Design detail for this package:

- Workspace: `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with catalogs for every shared dependency; `packages/protocol` as the first real package; empty-but-valid skeletons for the other P2 packages are not needed (generators create them when their WP starts), but the dependency-cruiser rules for the whole package map are written now.
- `@mostra/protocol`: branded ID types and parsers for every prefix in INTERFACES §1; dated revision type and negotiation helper (highest common revision, refusal diagnostic); the Diagnostic Zod schema with the area list from INTERFACES §13; JSON Schema 2020-12 and draft-07 emitters; the schema snapshot test that fails on any non-additive change (field removed, type narrowed, enum value removed, required added).
- Diagnostic catalog: codes declared in one source file per area; a generator emits the catalog JSON and one docs page per code (rendered later by the docs site, WP-26); a CI check fails on a code without docs text or on a removed code.
- Gates, each proven by a seeded violation in a test fixture: boundary import across the package map, unused export (knip), size budget, API report change without a changeset, non-additive schema change, non-OSI or PolyForm dependency in the core (license audit), unsigned commit (DCO), unpinned action (actionlint or pin check), Rust fmt and clippy, cargo-deny.
- CI: the plan job computing affected packages and the jobs in REPO_STANDARDS §6 that apply to what exists now (format-lint, types, unit, build, boundaries, api, licenses, rust, docs, supply-chain); later WPs add their suites to the existing jobs, not new workflow files. Measure the wall-clock of a typical pull request and record it.
- Port `tools/design/evidence_matrix.py` and `tools/design/wp_specs.py` into the docs CI job so the matrix and the WP specifications can never drift from the dossier.
- Local parity: `pnpm check`, `pnpm check --affected`, `pnpm fix`, `pnpm gen <name>` (generators for package, diagnostic code, protocol method; others are added by the WPs that need them), lefthook hooks.
- Documentation: root `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` (importing it) with commands, the package map, invariant owners, the WP workflow and the D49 agreements; `docs/agents/` playbooks for the tasks that exist now; README for humans; governance files. The root AGENTS.md text is agent-facing prose: draft it with Mirza (D74); WP-14 finalizes it.
- Rust: a cargo workspace with `crates/` placeholders only if needed for fmt/clippy/deny wiring; the crates themselves come in WP-12 and WP-22.

## Out of scope

- Product packages other than `@mostra/protocol` (WP-02 onward).
- The release workflow and publishing (WP-11); WP-01 only adds Changesets and the API gate.
- Final Skill and AGENTS.md prose (WP-14).

## Acceptance evidence

- CI green on a pull request, measured under 10 minutes, with parallel jobs visible;
- every gate shown to fail on a seeded violation (boundary import, unused export, license, API change without changeset, non-additive schema change, missing sign-off);
- `pnpm check` gives the same results as CI.

Also: `pnpm check` green (from WP-01 on), diff reviewed, evidence matrix rows updated, docs and AGENTS.md current, progress report written after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- Tool majors moved recently (pnpm 12, Vitest 5, TypeScript 7, Changesets 3): re-verify and add churn notes (D48).
- TypeScript 7 lacks the JS compiler API: API Extractor runs on a pinned TypeScript 6 (REPO_STANDARDS §4).
- Branch protection that requires checks before the checks exist can block your own merge: add required checks after the first green run.

## Publication

D76 authorizes it all: the repository `mostra-dev/mostra` exists with `main` pushed by the design session. Push `wp/01-foundation` and open a pull request early, so CI runs on GitHub while you work and its timing becomes evidence. Configure the repository: private vulnerability reporting, secret scanning with push protection, branch protection on `main` with the CI checks required and DCO enforced, Actions permissions read-only by default with SHA pinning, CODEOWNERS, labels, and Pages for the docs site (WP-26 deploys it). The protected `release` environment is WP-11's. Merge to `main` after Mirza accepts (D36). Record every setting you change in the progress report.

## Handoff

A green `main` with every gate live, `@mostra/protocol` at 0.x with IDs, revisions and diagnostics, generators and playbooks, and CI timing recorded. WP-02 adds the supervisor on top without touching the machinery.
